6: טוב אשר Better than one who did not vow  - Before that (i.e., that which was quoted) it is written "...one who vows [and] pays, and even the best of all is one who does not vow [in the first place], lest he vows and does not pay." This is how Rabbi Meir explains it.
טוב מזה Better than this one and that one  - Than one who vows and pays and who vows and does not pay.
שאינו Who does not vow whatsoever - For one who accustoms himself to making vows comes to eventually not fulfill his words.

רבי יהודה Rabbi Yehuda says, better than this one and that one is one who vows and pays - The implication here is that it is better not to vow than to vow and not pay, but one who vows and pays -- is he not better than all of them?

ואפילו And even Rabbi Yehuda only said so in relation to one who says, "Behold, this [animal is hereby consecrated]" - For if it dies or is stolen, he is not liable for it responsibility. Alternatively, since it can be brought out to pasture [until it develops a blemish], he can go back on it (i.e., a that point he may treat the animal as chullin without having broken his vow).
